What it does: How heavy the tank is. Shared with the kinematic tank.
Raise it: Slower to speed up, brake and turn; more momentum; settles harder on its springs

What it does: Top speed of each tread. The push fades to nothing as the treads reach it.
Raise it: Faster; run-ups carry further up slopes
Lower it: Slower; steep run-up climbs fail sooner

What it does: How hard the treads push (the real push is pulling power / weight). Also the brake's strength.
Raise it: Quicker off the line, stronger brake, climbs steeper from a standstill (up to the grip limit)
Lower it: Sluggish; the engine, not the grip, becomes what stops it on slopes

What it does: The steepest slope the treads can hold or climb from a standstill (a run-up can still beat it). Works at each of the 8 springs, so a lightly loaded corner grips less.
Raise it: Climbs and holds steeper slopes; less wheelspin
Lower it: Slips on slopes, spins the treads, slides back sooner

What it does: How much the tank resists sliding sideways (0 = ice, 1 = as firm as the tank allows).
Lower it: Drifts outward in turns and slides down side slopes

What it does: How high its weight sits (0.2 m at 0 to 2.2 m at 1). Real physics: changes rocking, leaning and rolling over.
Raise it: Rocks more when speeding up and braking, leans more in turns, tips off ledges more easily

What it does: How long each tread's push takes to build up from nothing to full when you ask for more power (0 = instant). Never delays the brake.
Raise it: Slower, heavier start; feels like a big engine winding up

What it does: How snappily the treads chase the lever's speed: push = (lever's speed - tread speed) x this, capped by pulling power. Decides how gently the push fades near the lever's speed and how gently the brake eases in near a stop.
Raise it: Snappier and harsher: full push until very close to the target speed, abrupt stops
Lower it: Softer: push fades over a wider speed range, braking eases in earlier

Unit: m/s lost per second, at weight 1
What it does: How hard a tread at lever 0 is held back by the idling engine. Decides how a lever at 0 swings the tank round that tread and how quickly it rolls to a stop with both levers at 0. Can't hold slopes steeper than about 18 degrees at 3 (the brake can).
Raise it: Tighter pivots on one lever, stops sooner when you let go, holds gentler slopes
Lower it: Coasts further, wider turns with a lever at 0

What it does: How strongly the treads resist being dragged sideways. This is what makes turning heavy (a turning tank drags the front and back of its treads sideways). Spin on the spot at 6 is about 44 degrees/s.
Lower it: Lighter, faster turning; more drift. Above about 30 it becomes unstable

What it does: Mass of a tank of weight 1. Not a knob: Weight already scales it, so changing both means the same thing twice.

How far the hull sinks onto its springs at rest; the springs' stiffness is worked out from this and the weight. Not a knob yet: changes the bounce and run-ups a little. Candidate later if suspension feel matters.
Raise it: Softer, bouncier springs; hull sits lower
Lower it: Stiffer, harsher springs; hull sits higher

What it does: How quickly the springs stop bouncing (1 = no bounce at all). Not a knob yet: candidate later with Target Sag.
Length of each spring with no weight on it; matched to the hull shape. Geometry, not feel.
Small always-on friction. Not a knob: Idle Drag does the noticeable slowing.
Raise it: Slows the tank slightly everywhere, also while driving

What it does: Used inside Sideways Grip's calculation. Not a knob: Sideways Grip is the knob for this.
Height of the weight at tippiness 0. Not a knob: Tippiness slides between this and High Centre Of Mass.
Height of the weight at tippiness 1. Not a knob: Tippiness is the knob.
Godot's general slowing of the whole body. A tiny stabiliser, not feel; at 0.1 it cost 0.25 m/s of top speed.
Godot's general slowing of the body's rotation. A tiny stabiliser against wobble, not feel.
Raise it: Turns and rocking die out sooner

What it does: How heavy it feels: divides the push, brake, idle drag, turn rate and tilt speed.
Raise it: Slower to speed up, brake and turn; coasts further

What it does: Top speed of each tread.
How hard the treads push (pulling power / weight); also the brake's strength.
Raise it: Quicker, stronger brake, climbs steeper from a standstill

What it does: Steepest slope it can hold or climb from a standstill (a run-up can beat it).
1 = no sideways slide in turns; lower = it drifts outward in fast turns.
How much the hull picture rocks, dips and leans (looks only; never moves the tank or the slit view).
Small always-on friction.

Unit: m/s lost per second, at weight 1
What it does: How hard a tread at lever 0 is held back (pivots on one lever; stops in about 3.2 s with both at 0).
Where the engine's push starts to fade toward top speed (1 = never fades). Only limits speeding up, never braking.
Lower it: Push fades from a lower speed

What it does: How much push is left at top speed (1 = no fade; 0 = never quite reaches top speed).
Lower it: Slower last stretch to top speed

What it does: Each tread's push builds up over this time when more power is asked for. Never delays the brake.
Gravity on slopes and in the air.
Distance between the treads (turning geometry).
How much turning is held back (above 1 would turn the wrong way).
While turning, the speed the treads can reach is divided by (1 + this x turn rate): turning costs speed. Straight driving is never affected.
Used inside Sideways Grip's calculation.
Gravity in the air only (jumps), not on slopes.
How much the hull picture tips to follow its flight path in the air.
Speed lost on a hard landing (a 10 m/s fall counts as fully hard).
How quickly the hull picture tilts to match the ground (looks only).

Unit: degrees per m/s per second, at tippiness 1
What it does: How far the hull picture sways per unit of speeding up, braking or turning (Tippiness scales it).
How far behind the tank the camera sits.
How high above the tank the camera sits (negative = below).
The point above the tank the camera aims at.
How quickly the camera catches up with the tank.
How quickly the aim point follows the tank up and down (calms the physics tank's bounce; 0 = no smoothing).
Lower it: Calmer view, lags more on ramps

What it does: Height of the open strip in the driver's vision-slit view.
Saved in: DriverSlitCamera node (Visual/Hull) in scenes/tank.tscn and scenes/physics_tank.tscn

What it does: Size of one height-image pixel on the ground (shows only in painted levels).
Saved in: LevelTerrain node in the level's scene

What it does: Height of pure white in the height image.
Saved in: LevelTerrain node in the level's scene

What it does: How many times the heights are softened (hides 8-bit steps).
Saved in: LevelTerrain node in the level's scene

Unit: x the tank's grip (tan of its angle)
What it does: How slippery mud is.
How much mud bogs the treads down.
Top speed in mud.
How far the hull picture sinks in (looks only).

Unit: x the tank's grip (tan of its angle)
What it does: How slippery sand is.
How much sand drags the treads.
Top speed on sand.
